$comment: What one section of a textbook yields, read out by a model: the concepts it names, how they stand to one another, what its figures show, and the terms it defines. The document twin of extraction.schema.json -- same shape (arrays of flat objects, relations as from/rel/to) so entities.fold folds it and the graph builder takes it without a second reader. A field the section does not give is an empty string, never a guess. `rel` and `kind` name a core vocabulary and accept any other name in the same snake_case shape; entities.fold_edges folds the spellings one book drifts into, and ingest.schema(core_only=True) fences both back to their core lists.

name.$comment: As the section writes it, singular where the section is.

kind.$comment: A snake_case kind. The ten in `examples` are the core set -- `unit` is a unit of measurement, `law` a named law, principle or theorem, `structure` a thing with parts, `process` something that happens over time -- and ingest.CORE_KINDS glosses each. A thing none of them fits takes a kind named in the same shape, and the fold marks the node `extension_kind`.

definition.$comment: One line, in the book's own words, only when the section defines it. Empty otherwise -- a definition invented here is the failure this field exists to make visible.

aliases.$comment: Other names the section itself uses for the same thing: a plural, an abbreviation, a symbol.

concepts.$comment: At most 96: a 2,500-token unit never needs more (the most seen was 75), and without a ceiling a greedy decode can circle the same entries -- one unit wrote 378 relations, 282 of them distinct, until n_predict cut it. The grammar closes the array; the model cannot loop.

rel.$comment: A snake_case verb phrase. The eighteen in `examples` are the core vocabulary, shared across every book and preferred wherever one of them states what the text states; ingest.VERBS glosses each and a test keeps the two lists equal. A relation none of them states is named in the same shape, and the fold marks the edge `extension`.

relations.$comment: At most 96: a 2,500-token unit never needs more (the most seen was 75), and without a ceiling a greedy decode can circle the same entries -- one unit wrote 378 relations, 282 of them distinct, until n_predict cut it. The grammar closes the array; the model cannot loop.

label.$comment: The book's own name for it, e.g. "Figure 2.9"; empty when the section gives none.

shows.$comment: What the picture shows, in one line.

concepts.$comment: Only the concepts the caption or the surrounding text says the figure illustrates. A concept guessed from the picture alone does not belong here.

figures.$comment: At most 16: a 2,500-token unit never needs more (the most seen was 75), and without a ceiling a greedy decode can circle the same entries -- one unit wrote 378 relations, 282 of them distinct, until n_predict cut it. The grammar closes the array; the model cannot loop.

key_terms.$comment: At most 64: a 2,500-token unit never needs more (the most seen was 75), and without a ceiling a greedy decode can circle the same entries -- one unit wrote 378 relations, 282 of them distinct, until n_predict cut it. The grammar closes the array; the model cannot loop.
